briefs.episode_title: Comex Silver.  What happened at the end of Jan? What about the March contract? Will May repeat?
briefs.one_line_summary: Comex silver registered stock is declining, and May deliveries will be interesting given high open interest.
core_claims: Registered or deliverable silver held in Comex warehouses is consistently declining.
Deliveries in March 2026 were well below available amounts and did not significantly change the Comex silver amount.
Projections show a continued downward trend in Comex silver inventory if the previous trend maintains.
May open interest is high, with 363 million ounces against Comex stocks around 79 million ounces.
briefs.positioning_implication: Monitor Comex silver inventories and delivery activity to assess potential supply constraints and market volatility. Be aware of potential scams impersonating the analyst.

briefs.one_line_summary: Cursor's AI model, Composer 2, is revealed to be based on Kimi K2.5, causing controversy over licensing and attribution.
core_claims: Cursor's Composer 2 model is based on Kimi K2.5, a Chinese open-source model.
Cursor failed to initially disclose the use of Kimi K2.5 as the base for their Composer 2 model, violating the license.
Cursor is utilizing Fireworks AI, an inference provider, to potentially circumvent the need to disclose the underlying Kimi K2.5 model.
Cursor spent 3/4 of compute on top of the existing kimi model.
Cursor utilizes self-summarization: where the model summarizes everything it knows, then continues with that compressed context.
Composer 2 was able to solve the 'make doom for mips' test
briefs.positioning_implication: Assess the implications of open-source AI models being rebranded and used in commercial products without proper attribution. Monitor geopolitical sensitivities related to AI technologies originating from specific countries.

briefs.episode_title: Gold to $7,000? Why This Correction Changes Nothing | Don Durrett & Andy Schectman
briefs.one_line_summary: Despite recent corrections, gold remains poised for a significant upward trajectory driven by underlying economic factors and monetary policy failures.
core_claims: The top of the mountain for gold is $7,000.
Silver will reach somewhere between $175 and $180, possibly ripping to $250-$280 at some point before falling back down.
The dollar is expected to devalue by 30-40% after the reset.
Gold's all-time high by the end of June is a firm belief.
briefs.positioning_implication: Increase allocation to physical gold and silver, and consider strategic investments in mining stocks. Diversify and prepare for potential devaluation of the dollar during the reset.

briefs.episode_title: McKinsey Says $1 Trillion In Sales Will Go Through AI Agents. Most Businesses Are Invisible.
briefs.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefs.one_line_summary: Companies must prioritize agent-readable/writable systems to capture future AI-driven commerce, requiring significant internal data stack changes.
core_claims: McKinsey projects AI agents will drive $1 trillion in US B2C retail revenue by 2030.
99% of future attention will be AI/agent-driven, demanding readable/writable infrastructure.
The traditional anti-bot web architecture is becoming obsolete, necessitating a shift to pro-bot systems.
The ability for agents to effectively discover, evaluate, and transact hinges on accessible, agent-readable transactional infrastructure.
Many companies resist agent readability due to fear of losing direct customer relationships and control.
briefs.positioning_implication: Re-evaluate data architecture to accommodate AI agents, or risk invisibility in future markets. Prioritize structured data and agent-accessible interfaces over traditional marketing.

briefs.episode_title: Gold, Silver Collapse, What’s Next? 'Fear Trade' Just Started | Gary Thompson
briefs.one_line_summary: Current market volatility is driven by a 'fear trade' rather than fundamental shifts, presenting a buying opportunity in metals.
core_claims: Gold and silver had unprecedented runs, with gold topping at $5500 an ounce and silver at above $100 an ounce.
The silver market is currently running into its sixth year of a deficit, with production not keeping up with demand and continued strength in demand from new applications.
Silver batteries using solid-state technology are slated to come to gadgets in 2026, and the real demand will come out in 2027, likely replacing Lithium-ion batteries.
Current market correction does not represent a correction in the fundamentals of metal demand; fundamentals that drove metal prices higher are still in place.
Brixston Metals' stock is up 85% YTD due to drilling at the Langus project, which it hasn't drilled since 2022, generating chart-topping drill results and interest from investors.
briefs.positioning_implication: Consider opportunities presented by market volatility, particularly in undervalued commodities, while acknowledging geopolitical risks.

briefs.episode_title: The Next Leg Up For Gold & Silver Start Soon - This Is Why!
briefs.one_line_summary: Gold and silver are poised for another upswing due to macro economic factors.
core_claims: Gold was never as high as it is right now measured in USD before December 22, 2025.
Fundamentals for gold and silver have not changed since the end of January.
The pullback is happening on the backdrop of an all out market correction.
Gold and silver enter their final leg up before a more significant pause.
Gold and silver performed best when oil prices rose significantly.
The U.S. government is rebuilding its strategic silver stockpile and paying above spot to secure it.
briefs.positioning_implication: Consider increasing or maintaining allocations to gold and silver, as current market corrections present potential buying opportunities before the next upswing. Watch for signals of aggressive interest rate cuts or rising inflation.

briefs.episode_title: Sun March 22, 2026 Financial Markets update. War, Hormuz, Oil, Dollar, stocks, gold, silver, miners.
briefs.one_line_summary: Market analysis reveals persistent Middle East crisis impacting oil prices, stock market declines, and dollar strength amidst falling precious metal values and rising bond yields.
core_claims: Oil prices are rising due to the Strait of Hormuz being effectively closed, with West Texas Intermediate crude at $98.10 and Brent crude at $107.84.
Stock markets had a rough week, with most major indices declining, except for the Nikkei 225 in Japan, which is still up on the year.
The US government 10-year bond yield started the year at 4.15 and is now at 4.38, indicating rising yields.
The dollar has risen sharply in the last few weeks, particularly since the end of January.
Gold miners' stocks are falling sharply despite good company results from Barrick, Agnico Eagle, etc.
US economy is slowing with job offers going down and GDP trends downwards since 2024.
briefs.positioning_implication: Reduce exposure to equities and precious metals; increase exposure to US dollar and consider hedging against rising interest rates. Diversify portfolio by underweighting equities and commodities in favor of cash and fixed income assets.

briefs.episode_title: A Market "Retrenchment" Ahead Looks Likely | Jonathan Wellum
briefs.one_line_summary: Markets face potential retrenchment due to rising energy costs, inflation, geopolitical tensions, and increasing interest rates, suggesting a possible global recession.
core_claims: Increasing energy costs will cause increasing inflation.
Further decoupling in the global economy is occurring due to the war in Iran.
Rising interest rates will negatively affect the overall economy, given its indebtedness.
briefs.positioning_implication: Reduce exposure to sectors vulnerable to rising costs and geopolitical uncertainty. Increase allocation to defensive assets and sectors benefiting from higher energy prices.
